subject: general
question: A sum of money, on compound interest, amounts to ₹578.40 in 2 years and to ₹614.55 in 3 years. The rate of interest per annum, in case of annual compounding, is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **annual compounding**, the **amount** at the end of a year acts as the **principal** for the following year.

Interest for the 3rd year = Amount (3 years) − Amount (2 years) = ₹614.55 − ₹578.40 = ₹36.15

Rate of Interest (R) = (Interest ÷ Principal) × 100

R = (36.15 ÷ 578.40) × 100 = (3615 ÷ 57840) × 100 = 6.25%

**∴ The correct answer is 6 ¼%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount after 2 years (A₂) = ₹578.40

Amount after 3 years (A₃) = ₹614.55

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/632c4f7be57410cdc8df8dc0592afd07e2b25ebe6694747187e20d7b698e13be.png] 

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ A₃ / A₂ = [P(1 + R/100)³] / [P(1 + R/100)²]

⇒ 614.55 / 578.40 = 1 + R/100

⇒ 1 + R/100 = 1.0625

⇒ R/100 = 1.0625 − 1 = 0.0625

⇒ R = 0.0625 × 100 = 6.25%

⇒ R = 6 ¼%

**∴ The correct answer is 6 ¼%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Basics

Compound interest is calculated on the principal plus any accumulated interest. Formula: A = P(1 + r/n)ⁿt.

Successive Growth

In annual compounding, the growth between any two consecutive years (Year n and Year n+1) is simply the annual rate R% of the amount at Year n.

Comparison with SI

For the first year, if compounding is annual, Simple Interest and Compound Interest on the same principal at the same rate are equal.
